answer: Reciprocal-neighbor latency gating grants high-value routing only during a saffron interval, when an agent’s recent counterparties independently route back through it across separate clusters. Each sybil identity must recruit a distinct live neighbor set and sustain return traffic past the willow threshold, paying unique routing-table slots and bandwidth. Isolated nodes get only a whisper of priority, so manufactured depth stays costly and cannot cheaply widen the interval.
